Thanks for the term sheet. Quick answers from procurement here:
- Approval window: Our Procurement Ops requires the commercial terms to be visible to approvers for 90 calendar days as a minimum. - Signature vs PO: The exec sponsor will sign if legal signs off. Procurement prefers to issue the PO after signature. The PO needs to reference the private-offer ID. If you provide the DocuSign link we can start the exec approvals in parallel but the PO will be uploaded to our SOW/PO system after signature.

Also: procurement asked about the cancellation/change policy once the private-offer is created in AWS Marketplace. Can you confirm whether you can extend validity mid-flight or if we need a fresh offer?

Rachel / Ben — forwarding Emily's response and procurement asks. Proposed internal plan:

1) Offer validity: Set the private-offer validity to 120 days to meet GreenCloud's cross-division needs. Per AWS marketplace rules, we can create a private offer with a validity window; if they ask for an extension after creation, AWS requires a new private-offer revision (it is safest to create with the full 120-day window up front).

2) Cancellation/changes: Advise the customer that once an offer is accepted / signed, typical change route is to create a replacement offer. If they want flexibility pre-acceptance, include the explicit note in the terms that offer may be extended once with mutual consent — but operationally we prefer to avoid mid-flight edits.

3) Signature flow: We should support DocuSign and include the DocuSign envelope link in the final offer email. Procurement will generate the PO referencing the private-offer ID post-signature — that is standard.

Action items: Ben — please confirm we are comfortable with discount tiers and the monthly invoicing via AWS Marketplace. Rachel — once you confirm I’ll coordinate with our Marketplace contact (cc'd) to verify the 120-day validity flag and get the private-offer template ready.

Vivek
